exact_missing_items: Define one canonical execution_unit_context owner doc, likely shared between Executor_Protocol.md and Prompt_Pipeline.md, then have storage/event/docs consume it by reference instead of cloning partial field sets
Keep any replacement for TierContext as a compatibility wrapper at most: legacy_decomposition_context plus canonical execution_unit_context — never the other way around
Migrate coordination and crew models from tier_id anchoring to canonical execution refs plus secondary labels (run_id, node_id, attempt_id, lane_id?, work_package_id?, feature_seam_id?)
Orchestrator_Page.md still keeps Tiers and multi-tab widget composition
Widget_System.md still catalogs tier widgets and weak hostability rules
storage-plan.md still splits tier-era event tables from newer attempt-centric records
execution_role and actor_role are used interchangeably across shard content — need one canonical name
execution_role is the preferred canonical name: it distinguishes the role the actor plays during this execution (not their long-lived identity role)
actor_role must be retired; all docs that reference actor_role must be updated to execution_role
storage-plan.md still leans on tier_id / run.tier_*
usage-feature.md still treats tier_id as a core attribution dimension and does not yet pivot to seam_id / package_id / lane_id
tier_id can still survive as a human-readable grouping label, but it should stop acting like the canonical execution correlation key
Tier-shaped surfaces may still display and group by tier_id, but they should resolve through pointers to canonical execution objects rather than using tier_id as if it were the durable execution key
Retarget Run Graph and Usage links toward node_id / attempt_id semantics, with tier_id surviving only as a display/grouping label where needed
stale_tokens: tier_id (as canonical orchestrator ownership key in coordination)
canonical_replacement_hints: attempt/node/lane/package/seam-aware attribution; tier terms only as compatibility aliases if needed
